reviews.review:
It has a cool setting and good mechanics but it's buggy and the storytelling is bad. It had so much potential.

6.5/10

Andromeda overall is alright... the main story is decent, but side quest are tedious and mostly fetch quest styled. The graphics and visuals are real nice, however the game feels unpolished, janky and buggy, the animations are stiff in cut-scenes and the dialogue also feels poor and not immersive.
The core gameplay is actually solid, combat is good with a lot of weapons and skills. Its not a great game but its also not terrible, its not worth the full price however.
Thumbs up because Steam doesn't have a middle options.

I don't think this game is nearly as bad as many reviews made it out to be. It's not perfect by any stretch and has its flaws but I still enjoyed it overall.

Granted, I bought the game on sale and played it after several patches. I went in with pretty low expectations and was surprised. 

The funny thing is that if I were to write out a list of positives and negatives, they'd probably be about equal in size but at the end of the day I had fun. The combat felt much improved over previous ME game, driving around and exploring in the Nomad felt much better than the original trilogy vehicles. The combat is my primary reason for giving this game a positive review.

Graphically it's mixed. The environments and worlds look great but the human faces in this game just look stiff and awkward. I'd highly recommend making your own character over going with the default characters. The alien faces look a little better.

Personally, I thought it was one of the best ME installments. Vivid character storylines, great combat action, decent inventory management/character skill development, and world-building questlines that make you feel like all your efforts are really making a difference for humanity every step of the way despite whatever moral ambiguity you may be faced with. Not to mention the great voice-acting, as per usual. Cora's voice always makes me fall in love all over again.
When I want to replay a ME experience, this is the one I usually come back to because I find it to be the most fun and interesting. Except the vaults. Vaults are jerks and overly complicated for no logical reason (activate these generic-looking consoles scattered around the facility in the exact right order to open up a specific path). Rather than feeling like a rat in a maze I just look up a video on how to do it. Not my idea of fun.
